RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: def introduces a definition. RealMainTheoremStatement is its name; : Prop says its value is a proposition, and := begins that proposition.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: We name the following statement RealMainTheoremStatement.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This is the statement corresponding to Theorem A, with the stronger uniform-convexity clause below. Defining it does not prove it; the closed declaration realMainTheorem proves this proposition.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: ∀ means “for every”; ρ : ℝ makes ρ a real number. Here → means implication: under the hypothesis 0 < ρ, everything to the right must hold.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: For every real $\rho>0$, the following witnesses and conclusions exist.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This is the opening “For every positive tolerance” of Theorem A. All subsequent choices may depend on this ρ; the same ρ is used in both norm bounds.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: ∃ means “there exists”. Here a specifies the two sequences in BlockParameters, satisfying all its conditions.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: Choose positive integers $N_j$ and real exponents $2<p_j\leq3$, with $p_{j+1}\leq p_j$ and $p_j\to2$.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: These are the sequences in Theorem A. Ambient a is the corresponding Banach space. Lean indexes the sequences from 0. Nonincreasing does not mean strictly decreasing.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: Ambient a applies the space construction Ambient to the chosen parameters a. The parentheses make it the argument of SeparableSpace. The final ∧ means “and”, joining this clause to all the following clauses.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: The space $X=(\bigoplus_j\ell_{p_j}^{N_j}(\mathbb R))_2$ is separable: it has a countable dense subset.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This requires the ambient space in Theorem A to be separable. Every later occurrence of Ambient a refers to this same choice of a.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: UniformConvexSpace means that the space is uniformly convex. Again ∧ means that this and the remaining conditions hold together.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: The existing norm of the same space $X$ is uniformly convex.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: The literal clause strengthens the displayed superreflexivity conclusion of Theorem A; the manuscript also establishes uniform convexity in Corollary 4.2(ii). The mathematical consequence “hence superreflexive” is distinct from what this Lean clause literally says.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: The project-defined predicate HasRealBanachLatticeOrder is applied to that same Ambient a. Its definition existentially chooses a lattice order; ∧ continues the conjunction.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: The space $X$, with its existing complete norm, admits a real vector-lattice order compatible with addition and nonnegative scalar multiplication, and the norm is solid: $|x|\leq|y|$ implies $\|x\|\leq\|y\|$.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This is the real Banach lattice condition in Theorem A. It chooses an order on X without replacing its norm or its scalar structure.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: ∃ P chooses a map. In X →L[ℝ] X, the spaces before and after the arrow are its domain and codomain; L and [ℝ] specify a continuous real-linear map.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: There exists a bounded real-linear operator $P:X\to X$.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This chooses the single operator used in every remaining clause. It introduces an operator; the next clause establishes that it is a projection.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: P.comp P is the composition of P with itself. = means equality of operators, and ∧ keeps the remaining requirements attached to the same P.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This is the projection requirement in Theorem A, not an additional choice of operator.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: The norm bars denote the operator norm of the bounded linear map P. < is a strict inequality, and ρ is the positive number fixed at the beginning.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This is the upper projection-norm bound in Theorem A(i); it constrains the P already chosen. The theorem does not choose a new tolerance here.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Ambient a) is the identity real-linear operator on X. Subtracting P forms another bounded operator; the surrounding norm bars take the norm of this entire difference.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This is the first additional requirement in Theorem A(ii). It holds for the same P and the same ρ as the preceding bound.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: Applying HasSeparatedRange to P substitutes P into a four-clause project definition. In that definition P.range is its range, →L[ℝ] ℝ is the continuous real dual, ⊤ is infinity, and ‖P‖ₑ is the operator norm in the extended nonnegative reals.
RealMainTheoremStatement.math: Put $Z=P(X)$. For both $V=Z$ and $V=Z^*$, $\chi_{\mathrm{GL}}(V)\leq\|P\|$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{DPR}}(V)=\infty$. The range carries the inherited norm and the continuous dual carries its operator norm.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: These are the four local-structure conclusions in Theorem A(i). Together with the earlier inequality they give the displayed chain χGL(V) ≤ ||P|| < 1+ρ. Idempotence is a separate requirement.

RealMainTheoremStatement.syntax: The parentheses give the whole operator I_X - P as the argument of the same predicate. Its definition therefore uses the range and norm of I_X - P throughout.
RealMainTheoremStatement.role: This completes Theorem A(ii). Both complementary ranges and both continuous duals satisfy separation simultaneously, for the one chosen X and P. The complementary GL bound is ||I_X-P||, not ||P||.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: def names a definition; : Prop says it is a proposition, and := introduces its full content.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: We name the real-field statement RealCorollaryStatement.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This proposition expresses the real case of Theorem B, including both nonlattice conclusions. The separate closed theorem realCorollary proves it.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: For every real number ρ, assume 0 < ρ. The implication arrow makes every subsequent existential and conjunction part of the conclusion under that assumption.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: The tolerance is arbitrary. The witnesses chosen next may depend on it.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: ∃ chooses a real Banach space X. X.Carrier is its underlying space; .{0} concerns the size of the type, not its vector-space dimension.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: There exists a real Banach space $X$.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This chooses the ambient space in the real case of Theorem B. All later basis and projection clauses refer to this one witness.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: The predicate takes the field ℝ and the underlying space X.Carrier as arguments. ∧ means this condition and the following ones must all hold.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: $X$ has an $\mathbb N$-indexed $1$-unconditional Schauder basis: every finite coordinate multiplier with real coefficients of modulus at most one is contractive.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This is the ambient basis in Theorem B. It is a basis with continuous coordinates and norm convergence, rather than only finite-dimensional local structure.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: ∃ P chooses a continuous real-linear endomorphism of the same underlying space X.Carrier. On normed spaces, such linear maps are bounded operators.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: There exists a bounded real-linear map $P:X\to X$.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: The remaining clauses constrain this one P and its one range; the next clause makes it a projection.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: comp denotes operator composition. The equality requires idempotence, and ∧ attaches all the remaining requirements to the chosen operator.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This is “a projection” in the real case of Theorem B.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: ‖P‖ is its operator norm; < makes the upper bound strict. The same positive ρ introduced above appears here.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This is the quantitative projection bound in Theorem B. This statement includes no norm bound for I-P.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: ¬ negates the whole basis-existence predicate. P.range denotes the range subspace, used with its inherited norm. ∧ continues the conjunction.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: The range $Z=P(X)$ admits no unconditional Schauder basis over $\mathbb R$, whether finite or indexed by $\mathbb N$.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This is the first negative basis conclusion of Theorem B. The predicate includes the empty basis of the zero space; this exclusion has no finite-dimensional loophole.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: The parenthesized type consists of continuous real-linear functionals on P.range. ¬ again denies existence of either kind of unconditional Schauder basis.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: The continuous real dual $Z^*=\mathcal B_{\mathbb R}(Z,\mathbb R)$, with its operator norm, admits no unconditional Schauder basis.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This is the second negative basis conclusion, for the dual of the same range Z. It is not a claim about the algebraic dual.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: The negated project predicate would choose some complete real Banach-space model with a compatible lattice order and a bounded real-linear isomorphism from P.range to that model.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: $Z=P(X)$ is not isomorphic, as a real Banach space, to any real Banach lattice.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This is the first extra conclusion for the real field in Theorem B. It excludes all target lattice norms, not only lattice orders on Z with its present norm; the isomorphism need not preserve order.

RealCorollaryStatement.syntax: The same negated isomorphism-existence predicate is now applied to the continuous real dual of P.range.
RealCorollaryStatement.math: $Z^*$ is not isomorphic, as a real Banach space, to any real Banach lattice.
RealCorollaryStatement.role: This completes the real case of Theorem B. All four exclusions concern the range of the single chosen projection and its continuous dual.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: def names a proposition depending on the field 𝕜. (𝕜 : Type*) specifies the scalar type, the square-bracketed argument requires a nontrivially normed field structure on it, : Prop identifies a proposition, and := begins its body.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.math: For a fixed nontrivially normed scalar field $\mathbb K$, define the following unconditional-basis statement.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This statement covers both scalar fields. Defining it for general 𝕜 does not prove it for every field. The selected theorems prove it over ℝ and, through ComplexCorollaryStatement, over ℂ.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: ∀ quantifies over real tolerances ρ, even when the space has complex scalars. The implication assumes positivity and governs the entire remaining conclusion.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.math: For every real $\rho>0$, the following witnesses exist.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This is the opening quantifier of Theorem B for the fixed scalar field. Space and projection can depend on ρ.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: ∃ chooses a BanachModel over the same field 𝕜. That structure specifies a normed vector space and completeness; .{0} concerns the type universe, not finite dimensionality.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.math: There exists a Banach space $X$ over $\mathbb K$.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This is the ambient-space witness of Theorem B. X.Carrier denotes this chosen space in the later clauses.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: Apply the project basis-existence predicate to the chosen field and space. ∧ means that this and the subsequent clauses all hold for the same witness.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.math: $X$ has an $\mathbb N$-indexed $1$-unconditional Schauder basis. Every finite coordinate multiplier with $\mathbb K$-valued coefficients of modulus at most one is contractive.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This gives the ambient basis. For 𝕜 = ℂ it includes all complex phases, not merely real signs; for 𝕜 = ℝ it uses real multipliers.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: ∃ introduces P and →L[𝕜] makes it a continuous 𝕜-linear map from the chosen space to itself.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.math: There exists a bounded $\mathbb K$-linear operator $P:X\to X$.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This is the single operator for all remaining requirements. In the complex case it is complex-linear, not only real-linear.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: P.comp P composes the operator with itself. Equality to P requires idempotence, and ∧ continues the joint requirements.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This is “a projection” in Theorem B, for the fixed field.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: The norm bars denote the operator norm, < is strict, and ρ is the real tolerance fixed above.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This is the near-one upper bound in Theorem B. No strict lower bound 1 < ||P|| or complementary projection bound is a clause of this proposition.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: ¬ negates existence of a basis. P.range is the range of the chosen 𝕜-linear map, with its inherited norm; the basis predicate uses this same scalar field.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.math: $Z=P(X)$ admits no unconditional Schauder basis over $\mathbb K$, finite or indexed by $\mathbb N$.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This is the first exclusion in Theorem B. The finite case, including the empty basis of the zero space, is included in the negated predicate.

UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.syntax: The parenthesized type is the space of continuous 𝕜-linear maps from P.range to 𝕜. The outer predicate is negated, so this dual space has no basis of either permitted index type.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.math: The continuous dual $Z^*=\mathcal B_{\mathbb K}(Z,\mathbb K)$, with its operator norm, admits no unconditional Schauder basis over $\mathbb K$.
UnconditionalCorollaryStatement.role: This completes the basis conclusion for both Z and its continuous dual. With 𝕜 = ℂ the functionals are complex-linear. This template adds no nonlattice or GL/DPR conclusion.

ComplexCorollaryStatement.syntax: def introduces a named proposition. : Prop gives its kind and := introduces what it means.
ComplexCorollaryStatement.math: We name the complex-field statement ComplexCorollaryStatement.
ComplexCorollaryStatement.role: The closed theorem complexCorollary proves this proposition. The definition itself is not a proof.

ComplexCorollaryStatement.syntax: Set 𝕜 = ℂ in the shared proposition. This defines the complex case without adding any assumptions.
ComplexCorollaryStatement.math: For every real $\rho>0$, there exist a complex Banach space $X$ with a $1$-unconditional Schauder basis and a complex-linear projection $P:X\to X$ with $\|P\|<1+\rho$, such that neither $Z=P(X)$ nor its continuous complex dual $Z^*$ admits an unconditional Schauder basis.
ComplexCorollaryStatement.role: This is the complex case of Theorem B. Read the full UnconditionalCorollaryStatement body with 𝕜 = ℂ beside this alias: its quantifiers, conjunctions and both negations all remain in force. Ambient multipliers include complex phases; basis exclusions include finite bases. No complex GL/DPR or complex nonlattice conclusion is added.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: def names a proposition, : Prop identifies it as a proposition, and := begins its content.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: We name the following statement of a counterexample to primariness.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: The theorem realSeparableNonprimarity proves this proposition. It provides a concrete counterexample for Corollary C rather than defining a general “primary class” predicate.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: ∀ ranges over real ρ. Under the positivity hypothesis, the implication requires all the following witnesses and properties.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: The quantitative witness can be chosen for every positive tolerance. Both projection bounds below use this same ρ.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: ∃ chooses a real Banach space. X.Carrier is its underlying space. The .{0} annotation fixes the type universe; it does not mean that the dimension is zero.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: There exists a real Banach space $X$.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This is the single ambient space of the counterexample. It may depend on ρ, and all the following properties concern this same X.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: The library separability predicate is applied to the underlying space X. The final ∧ requires this and the remaining clauses together.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: $X$ is separable: it has a countable dense subset.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This puts the ambient example in the separable setting of Corollary C.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: This project predicate chooses a compatible real lattice order on the existing complete normed space X.Carrier. It does not choose a new ambient norm.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: $X$ is a real Banach lattice in its given norm: the order respects the vector-space operations and the norm is solid.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This places the ambient example in the class whose primariness is disproved. The two summands will fail membership even up to isomorphism.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: The project predicate takes the field ℝ and X.Carrier. Its definition chooses a complete uniformly convex normed real space H and a continuous linear equivalence between X and H.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: $X$ is isomorphic to a complete uniformly convex real normed space; equivalently, it has an equivalent uniformly convex norm.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This is the superreflexivity convention used for the quantitative Corollary C witness. It is a renormability condition, distinct from a literal UniformConvexSpace X clause.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: The project predicate specifies an ℕ-indexed real unconditional Schauder basis and requires all finite coordinate multipliers of modulus at most one to be contractions.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: The ambient space $X$ has a $1$-unconditional Schauder basis.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This adds the ambient basis promised by the explicit witness in Corollary 4.5, p.22. It is compatible with all the preceding conditions on the same X.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: ∃ P chooses a continuous real-linear operator on the underlying space X, which is the same real Banach space fixed above.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: There exists a bounded real-linear map $P:X\to X$.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: The following idempotence, two norm inequalities and two negations all concern this single P.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: comp means operator composition. This equality makes P idempotent; ∧ continues the conjunction.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: $P^2=P$. Hence $P$ and $I_X-P$ are complementary projections and $X=P(X)\oplus(I_X-P)(X)$.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This gives the complemented decomposition used to refute primariness. Because P is bounded, both summands are closed.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: Take the operator norm of P and compare it strictly with 1 + ρ, using the tolerance chosen at the start.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This controls the first projection in the quantitative nonprimarity witness.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X.Carrier is I_X. Subtraction forms I_X - P before its operator norm is taken. The same ρ appears in the strict upper bound.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This controls the complementary projection simultaneously; no new operator or tolerance is chosen.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: P.range is the first range with its inherited norm. ¬ negates existence of any complete real Banach lattice model and a bounded real-linear isomorphism from this range to that model.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: $P(X)$ is not isomorphic to any real Banach lattice.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: This excludes the first summand from the lattice class, even after a change of norm. The isomorphism in the negated predicate is a Banach-space isomorphism; it need not preserve order.

SeparableNonprimarityStatement.syntax: The parentheses form I_X - P, and .range then takes its range. The same isomorphism-existence predicate is negated for this second subspace. The physical line break does not split the clause.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.math: $(I_X-P)(X)$ is not isomorphic to any real Banach lattice.
SeparableNonprimarityStatement.role: Together with the preceding exclusion, this gives a separable real Banach lattice decomposed into two closed summands, neither isomorphic to a Banach lattice: the counterexample in Corollary C. This exact statement does not add nonlattice conclusions for the summands’ duals.
